status_summary: No executive order extending export control authority to personal data, and no BIS rule implementing one, was found: a Federal Register API query of BIS documents since 2025-01-20 for personal data returned no results. A parallel measure of different design exists: a Justice Department rule under Executive Order 14117 of 2024-02-28, issued under IEEPA, prohibits or restricts transactions giving countries of concern access to bulk U.S. sensitive personal data. It was published 2025-01-08, before the period tracked, with a stated effective date of 2025-04-08 and further compliance duties from 2025-10-06. It is administered by the Justice Department, not BIS.
title: Restrict exports of U.S. persons' personal data to countries of concern by executive order
uncertainties: The negative finding rests on a Federal Register API term search of BIS documents and the earlier researcher's one web search; it is not a systematic review. Whether the Justice Department rule took effect on its stated date without change, and how it has been enforced since, were not checked; it is a prior-administration measure and is cited as a parallel, not as a qualifying action. The query used for the BIS check is recorded in the review, not as a source. Checked systematically on 2026-10-18: Federal Register search of BIS documents for personal data, Unified Agenda route via the proposed-rule listing for BIS (zero), a congress.gov and GovInfo search with BILLSTATUS read of one privacy bill, the BIS newsroom, and one news search found no executive order or BIS rule extending export controls to personal data. The only Justice Department action on the parallel data security rule since 2025-01-20 found in the Federal Register is a correction of a cross-reference published 2025-04-18. The Unified Agenda agency listing could not be browsed and the enacted 119th Congress laws were not read for data-export provisions.
